title: DrugCLIP screens about 10,000 human proteins against 500 million compounds
summary: Contrastive learning, reported up to 10 million times faster than docking, gave wet-lab hit rates of 15% for the norepinephrine transporter and 17.5% for thyroid hormone receptor interactor 12, with two inhibitor structures solved. Hit rates cover a small set of targets; most of the genome-wide screen is computational.

evidence.tested: Wet-lab testing of computational hits: 15% hit rate for the norepinephrine transporter and 17.5% for thyroid hormone receptor interactor 12 using AlphaFold2 structures; two inhibitor structures solved.
evidence.unknown: Wet-lab validation covers two targets; most of the genome-wide screen is computational; generalizability is an open question.
evidence.ai_role: Contrastive learning framework for ultrafast virtual screening of about 10,000 human proteins against 500 million compounds.
